title: Ethics: how should we live?
audience: a high-school student (grades 9–12) or an adult reviewing high-school work
purpose: Examine the main ethical theories (consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contract theory, care ethics and natural law), ask whether moral claims can be true, and apply the theories to questions about honesty, animals, the environment, wealth and poverty, technology and justice, presenting each side fairly.
primary_reading: OpenStax Introduction to Philosophy: the chapters on value theory, normative moral theory and applied ethics (free)

weeks.1: What ethics studies: moral questions and moral reasoning
weeks.6: Social contract theory and care ethics
weeks.8: Metaethics: can moral claims be true?
weeks.9: Applied ethics: animals and the environment
weeks.10: Applied ethics: wealth, poverty and what we owe others
weeks.11: Applied ethics: technology, privacy and AI

blocks.deliverable: Explain the difference between describing a practice and judging it.
Apply both theories to the same case about lying.
Compare how three theories judge a dilemma between friends.
Week 7 midterm; reconstruct an argument for or against moral realism.
Write a balanced analysis of an argument about a duty to give aid.
Write a balanced essay on one applied question.
Submit the project; take an unseen 60 minute final in week 14.

project: Ethics case study: choose one contested practical question from the course, set out the strongest case on each side with at least two ethical theories, answer the main objections, and write a 1,500-word essay that defends a conclusion while treating the other side fairly.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
